title: OSCORE Appendix B.2 kid_context 的 CBOR 包装缓冲区空间少算 1 字节
label: TP
evidence: src/oscore/oscore.c:221 writes through ptr=&option_buffer[offset+1] but passes rem_space unchanged
src/oscore/oscore.c:226-231 subtracts 1 after oscore_cbor_put_bytes(), which underflows when the CBOR header plus kid_context exactly fills rem_space
src/oscore/oscore_cbor.c:104-118 copies bytes_len when the remaining counter equals bytes_len, so the last byte lands at option_buffer[255]
src/coap_oscore.c:418 declares uint8_t oscore_option[255]; src/coap_oscore.c:541 enables B.2 encoding when b_2_step != COAP_OSCORE_B_2_NONE
src/coap_oscore.c:1209-1234 stores an attacker-influenced R2||ID1 value as id_context that is later encoded
reason: Appendix B.2 CBOR wrapping advertises one byte more than is available at the shifted pointer; an aligned kid_context writes index 255, underflows rem_space, and lets the following key-id copy run past the 255-byte stack array. Reachable when B.2 mode is enabled.

title: Uri-Path-Abbrev 回退重传时载荷被加到旧 PDU 并随旧 PDU 释放
label: TP
evidence: src/coap_net.c:1801-1808 duplicates the request into new, then calls coap_add_data(pdu, ...) on the old PDU and frees that old PDU
src/coap_pdu.c:233-235 documents that coap_pdu_duplicate_lkd() copies only token and options, not data
src/coap_block.c:5191-5196 shows the correct pattern, adding the saved body to the new duplicate
reason: Once no_path_abbrev is set, the fallback retransmit adds the body to the PDU that is immediately deleted, so the transmitted duplicate carries no payload. This silently changes request integrity for body-bearing requests on sessions using Uri-Path-Abbrev.

title: coap_ws_close 用 100 字节栈缓冲复读未完成 WebSocket 帧
label: TP
evidence: src/coap_ws.c:697-707 is the only frame-size check and compares against the datalen of the header-parsing call
src/coap_ws.c:762-764 resumes with l_read(&data[data_ofs], data_size-data_ofs) without rebounding to the caller-supplied datalen
src/coap_ws.c:900-914 calls coap_ws_read(session, buf, sizeof(buf)) with uint8_t buf[100] during close drain
src/coap_ws.c:681 keeps all_hdr_in set for a partially received frame
reason: A partial frame leaves all_hdr_in set with data_size larger than the close-drain buffer. The resume path asks l_read for data_size-data_ofs bytes into the 100-byte stack buffer, giving a concrete attacker-controlled stack overwrite when WebSocket support and a WS endpoint are enabled and close timing is met.

title: 单字节 WebSocket Close 载荷读取未初始化字节
label: TP
evidence: src/coap_ws.c:720-729 enters the close branch when the received close-frame length is 1 and computes close_reason from data[0] and data[1]
src/coap_ws.c:729 reads data[1] even though only one byte was copied into the caller buffer
src/coap_ws.c:899-914 later sends close_reason back to the peer
reason: A 1-byte WebSocket Close payload makes the code read an uninitialized byte and echo it as part of the close reason. The defect is real but discloses only a single byte to the same peer; WebSocket support is required.

title: OSCORE 响应侧短密文路径未回滚重放窗口（拒绝服务）
label: TP
evidence: src/coap_oscore.c:1370-1382 validates and advances rcp_ctx->last_seq before AEAD verification on the response path
src/coap_oscore.c:1482-1501 short-ciphertext response branch logs the failure and jumps to error without oscore_roll_back_seq()
src/coap_oscore.c:1541-1551 other decryption failure paths do call oscore_roll_back_seq()
src/oscore/oscore.c:434-478 records rollback state before advancing the window
reason: The response replay window is advanced before authentication, and the encrypt_len <= tag_len response branch omits the rollback present in adjacent failure paths. An on-path attacker who can forge a short high-PIV response matching the token can make later genuine responses look like replays.

title: coap_rebuild_pdu_for_proxy 移除 Proxy-Uri 后使用旧指针
label: FP
evidence: src/coap_oscore.c:288-322 parses Proxy-Uri, removes the option, then uses uri.host/path/query to build new options
src/coap_uri.c:256,331,340 set uri fields to point into the Proxy-Uri option value inside the PDU buffer
src/coap_pdu.c:635-639 memmove stays within the same PDU allocation and only shrinks used_size
src/coap_oscore.c:296-322 uses lengths bounded by the original option value
reason: The stale pointers remain within the existing PDU allocation and removal only shifts bytes within that allocation; no out-of-bounds access follows. Any wrong target bytes come from the attacker's own Proxy-Uri/PDU, so this is a correctness issue without a security-relevant path.

title: 代理 Hop-Limit 缺省与端点比较问题
label: UNKNOWN
evidence: src/coap_pdu.c:887-895 inserts a default Hop-Limit of 255 when a Proxy-Uri or Proxy-Scheme option is added
src/coap_net.c:3976-3980 only validates Hop-Limit when present
src/coap_net.c:4094-4113 only decrements when hop_limit >= 0
src/coap_net.c:3954-3958 uses case-sensitive coap_string_equal for proxy endpoint matching
reason: The report is too vague to map to a concrete loop or amplification path. A default Hop-Limit insertion exists for library-generated proxy options, and the residual case-sensitivity/self-loop concern depends on a specific proxy deployment that cannot be resolved from the snapshot.

title: %2F 主机被解析为本地 AF_UNIX 目标
label: UNKNOWN
evidence: src/coap_uri.c:260-264 treats a %2F host prefix as a Unix-domain definition
src/coap_uri.c:474-484 coap_host_is_unix_domain() also accepts hosts beginning with '/'
src/coap_address.c:749-770 resolves such hosts via coap_address_set_unix_domain()
src/coap_proxy.c contains no guard rejecting Unix-domain targets for dynamic forwarding
reason: The %2F-to-Unix-socket parsing is explicit and intentional, and no proxy guard blocks it, but security impact depends on whether an exposed FWD_DYNAMIC proxy is deployed and whether local Unix sockets are sensitive. That runtime/deployment fact is not resolvable from the snapshot.

title: Request payload silently dropped when retransmitting Uri-Path-Abbrev requests (coap_net.c)
label: TP
evidence: src/coap_net.c:1801-1808 adds the body to the old PDU and frees it instead of adding it to new
src/coap_pdu.c:233-235 states duplication copies only token and options, not data
src/coap_block.c:5191-5196 shows the intended add-to-new-PDU behavior
reason: Same root cause as the Mygoldmine report: the Uri-Path-Abbrev fallback builds a duplicate without payload and writes the payload to the discarded original PDU, silently dropping request bodies.

title: Unauthenticated memory exhaustion in OSCORE Appendix B.2 context handling
label: TP
evidence: src/coap_oscore.c:1109-1122 calls oscore_duplicate_ctx() for an unknown kid_context before AEAD verification
src/oscore/oscore_context.c:743-746 oscore_enter_context() links the duplicate into c_context->p_osc_ctx
src/coap_oscore.c:1856-1867 error/error_no_ack releases associations and PDUs but never unlinks or frees the duplicated context
src/oscore/oscore_context.c:996-1008 only frees an unattached context on recipient release
reason: Each unauthenticated B.2 request with a fresh kid_context leaves a duplicated security context linked to the CoAP context after decryption fails. Repetition grows the chain without bound when B.2 is enabled and a valid recipient KID is known.

title: NULL pointer dereference in OSCORE external credential lookup crashes the server
label: TP
evidence: src/oscore/oscore_context.c:371-396 assigns *recipient_ctx only on a KID match, then still returns tmp_ctx with *recipient_ctx left NULL when a multi-recipient set has no match
src/coap_oscore.c:1064-1068 expects oscore_find_context() to fill rcp_ctx, initialized to NULL
src/coap_oscore.c:1146-1157 calls the setter and dereferences rcp_ctx->initial_state before AEAD verification
examples/coap-server.c:3196-3197 registers the external find handler via coap_oscore_register_external_handlers()
reason: With the documented external credential callback and a multi-recipient (or zero-recipient) credential set lacking the request KID, the lookup returns a non-NULL context but a NULL recipient, and the request path dereferences it before authentication.

title: Uninitialised heap memory disclosed through re-assembled Block1 body when the block size grows mid-transfer
label: TP
evidence: src/coap_block.c:3604 computes offset from the current request's block.szx
src/coap_block.c:3693-3697 records the transfer SZX in lg_srcv->szx but no later check compares block.szx to it
src/coap_block.c:4050-4058 hands pdu->body_data with body_length = lg_srcv->total_len to the application
src/coap_block.c:4594-4596 allocates with coap_new_binary(), and src/coap_str.c:42-46 zeroes only the union header, not the payload area
src/coap_block.c:4620-4624 copies only the current segment, leaving any gap uninitialized
reason: A client that increases SZX between Block1 blocks makes the next offset jump past received data; reassembly still marks the transfer complete and hands the application total_len bytes with an uninitialized heap gap. Requires server-side single-body/Q-Block reassembly.

title: heap_buffer_overflow at src/coap_block.c:1879
label: UNKNOWN
evidence: src/coap_block.c:1867-1880 ignores coap_add_token() and coap_add_option_internal() results and unconditionally writes pdu->token[pdu->used_size++]
src/coap_pdu.c:439-446 lets a token bring used_size exactly to max_size
src/coap_pdu.c:395-412 refuses further growth past max_size without changing used_size
src/coap_block.c:3542-3547 requires Q-Block1 requests to carry Size1 and RTag before this path
src/coap_pdu.c:139 sets alloc_size=min(size, COAP_DEFAULT_MTU) while max_size may be larger, so reachability depends on transport/CSM sizing
reason: The unchecked marker write is real, but the reported default-UDP trigger is statically contradicted: the incoming request and the 4.08 response share the same PDU size limit and the mandatory Size1/RTag options leave no room for a PDU-filling token. Other transport/CSM/extended-token paths may exist but are not established from the snapshot.

title: WebSocket close path can overflow a 100-byte stack buffer with a partial frame
label: TP
evidence: src/coap_ws.c:697-707 checks the frame size only against the current call's datalen and leaves all_hdr_in set on a partial frame
src/coap_ws.c:762-764 requests data_size-data_ofs bytes from l_read on resumption without rebounding to the new datalen
src/coap_ws.c:900-914 drains with uint8_t buf[100] and calls coap_ws_read(session, buf, sizeof(buf))
reason: Same root cause as the Mygoldmine report: a partial WebSocket frame plus close-drain re-entry with a 100-byte buffer lets the stale frame size drive an out-of-bounds stack write.

title: OSCORE external credential lookup can return a context with no recipient and crash the server
label: TP
evidence: src/oscore/oscore_context.c:371-396 returns tmp_ctx after freeing all recipients when none matches, leaving *recipient_ctx NULL
src/coap_oscore.c:1064-1068 passes rcp_ctx initialized to NULL into the lookup
src/coap_oscore.c:1146-1157 dereferences rcp_ctx->initial_state without checking rcp_ctx
reason: Same root cause as the Strix report: an external multi-recipient credential set without the request KID yields a non-NULL context with a NULL recipient, which the request path dereferences before authentication.

title: OSCORE Appendix B.2 kid_context encoder writes past the 255-byte stack buffer and underflows its remaining-space counter
label: TP
evidence: src/oscore/oscore.c:221-231 shifts the write pointer by one but passes the unshifted rem_space and then can underflow it
src/oscore/oscore_cbor.c:104-118 copies bytes_len once the remaining counter equals bytes_len
src/oscore/oscore.c:247-254 the key-id bound check is bypassed after rem_space underflows to SIZE_MAX
src/coap_oscore.c:418 holds the 255-byte stack buffer; src/coap_oscore.c:541 invokes B.2 encoding
reason: Same root cause as the Mygoldmine report: the B.2 CBOR wrapper under-accounts by one byte, allowing a one-byte stack write and then an unbounded key-id copy after the counter underflow.

title: Block1 reassembly can hand uninitialized heap bytes to the application
label: TP
evidence: src/coap_block.c:3604 derives the write offset from the current block.szx
src/coap_block.c:3693-3697 stores lg_srcv->szx but never rejects a later block with a different SZX
src/coap_block.c:4594-4596 allocates the body without zeroing; src/coap_str.c:42-46 zeroes only the header
src/coap_block.c:4050-4058 hands total_len bytes to the application even though only received segments were copied
reason: Same root cause as the Strix report: a mid-transfer SZX increase creates a never-written gap in the reassembled body, which is then exposed to the application with the full total length.

title: Appendix B.2 creates unbounded OSCORE contexts before authentication
label: TP
evidence: src/coap_oscore.c:1109-1122 duplicates the context before the AEAD tag is verified
src/oscore/oscore_context.c:743-746 links the duplicate into the global CoAP context chain
src/coap_oscore.c:1856-1867 frees only associations and PDUs on failure, not the duplicated context
reason: Same root cause as the Strix report: unauthenticated B.2 requests with fresh kid_context values accumulate permanently linked OSCORE contexts, causing unbounded memory growth.

title: Short OSCORE responses advance the replay window without rollback
label: TP
evidence: src/coap_oscore.c:1370-1382 advances rcp_ctx->last_seq before AEAD verification on responses
src/coap_oscore.c:1482-1501 the short-ciphertext response branch omits oscore_roll_back_seq()
src/coap_oscore.c:1541-1551 the generic decrypt-failure path does roll back
reason: Same root cause as the Mygoldmine report: an on-path attacker can advance the response replay window with a forged short high-PIV response, causing later genuine responses to be rejected.

title: pdu_408_build writes the payload marker without checking capacity
label: UNKNOWN
evidence: src/coap_block.c:1867-1880 writes the payload marker unconditionally after ignoring token and option add results
src/coap_pdu.c:439-446 permits an exact-fill token and src/coap_pdu.c:395-412 refuses further growth
src/coap_block.c:3542-3547 requires Size1 and RTag on Q-Block1 requests, reducing room for a PDU-filling token
src/coap_pdu.c:139 sets alloc_size=min(size, COAP_DEFAULT_MTU) while max_size can be larger, so transport/CSM sizing determines reachability
reason: The one-byte unchecked marker write is real, but the report itself calls it latent and the default-UDP path is blocked by the shared PDU limit plus mandatory Q-Block1 options. Whether a TCP/CSM or other configuration admits a PDU-filling token is a runtime/transport fact not settled by the snapshot.

title: Uri-Path-Abbrev fallback retransmit drops the request body
label: TP
evidence: src/coap_net.c:1801-1808 adds the payload to the old PDU and frees it, while new is sent without data
src/coap_pdu.c:271-281 duplication copies options but not payload
src/coap_block.c:5191-5196 demonstrates the correct target for the re-added body
reason: Same root cause as the Mygoldmine report: the fallback retransmit attaches the request body to the discarded PDU, so the expanded request on the wire silently loses its payload.
